videos.title: Creating A New Universal Standard For Refueling Spacecraft
videos.description:
Spaceium (S24) is building fully automated refueling stations in orbit so spacecraft can keep working instead of being discarded when they run out of fuel. Today, the company is announcing OpenPort, an open-standard refueling interface for spacecraft. For just $1, companies can license Spaceium's tech to build their own ports.

In this episode of Founder Firesides, co-founders Ashi Dissanayake and Reza Fetanat discuss why their business is selling fuel, not ports, and how they use AI, in-house manufacturing, and repeated testing to build space hardware faster and more cheaply. They also share their journey from a laundry room to their first mission in orbit, plus plans for a xenon fuel-transfer test outside the International Space Station in 2027 and their first refueling station launch in 2028.

https://spaceium.com

videos.title: How Model ML Is Building the AI Operating System For Finance
videos.description:
Model ML (W24) is building the AI operating system for financial services, used by the largest banks, asset managers, and consulting firms in the world. Eighteen months after coming out of stealth, they’ve gone from 10 people to 200 across eight offices, and they’re still adding about 20 a week.

At YC x London, co-founder and CEO Chaz Englander sat down with YC’s Gustaf Alströmer to talk about why agent harnesses couldn’t work with Excel until February, how to get investors to tell you the truth about why they passed, and why he thinks every founder in Europe is being insufficiently ambitious.

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
videos.description:
A coding agent opens a pull request and picks an email provider for you. How did it choose? Resend co-founder and CEO Zeno Rocha explores answer engine optimization (AEO) through a concrete example: which email provider does Claude Code recommend, and how does that change across model versions? Then comes the agent experience itself. Once the agent picks Resend, can it find the price, set up the account and send its first email?

We also follow an email after the API call succeeds. Zeno explains what happens when Gmail throttles a burst, why a tracking pixel can give you the wrong idea about who opened a message, and how one abusive sender can put other customers’ mail at risk. Then we get into the product decisions: giving an agent 80+ named MCP tools, letting it read pricing in Markdown, and letting it register for a service on its own.

Explore the references
• Zeno’s analysis of what Claude Code recommends: https://x.com/zenorocha/status/2027757871597822022
• Resend’s $3M email safety pledge: https://resend.com/blog/3-million-to-make-email-safer
• React Email, the open-source email components: https://react.email/
• The proposed agent registration standard shown on screen: https://workos.com/auth-md
